meta.note: IMPORTANT: Please proofread all player data before launch. Verify clues, stats, and fun facts for accuracy.

players.name: Sachin Tendulkar
clues: Debuted in 1989 at age 16 against Pakistan and played for over 24 years.
A right-hand batter who played over 600 international matches across formats.
Represented Mumbai in domestic cricket and played for a franchise in Mumbai in the IPL.
Holds the record for most international centuries by any cricketer.
First player to score a double century in ODI cricket (200* vs South Africa in 2010).
Known as the 'Master Blaster' and wore jersey number 10.
players.funFact: He was carried on shoulders after India's 2011 World Cup win. Virat Kohli said, 'Tendulkar carried Indian cricket for 22 years, it was time we carried him.'

players.name: Virat Kohli
clues: Debuted in 2008 and captained his country's U-19 World Cup winning side.
A right-hand batter regarded as one of the best chasers in ODI history.
Captained India across all three formats of the game.
Has scored over 75 international centuries across formats.
Played his entire IPL career for one franchise based in Bangalore.
Known as 'King Kohli' and wears jersey number 18.
players.funFact: He scored his 50th ODI century in the 2023 World Cup, equalling Sachin Tendulkar's record in a World Cup match.

players.name: MS Dhoni
clues: Debuted in 2004 and played international cricket until 2020.
A wicketkeeper-batter known for finishing matches under pressure.
Led his country to victories in all three major ICC trophies.
Famous for a six to win the 2011 Cricket World Cup final.
Captained a franchise based in Chennai to multiple IPL titles.
Known as 'Captain Cool' and wears jersey number 7.
players.funFact: His last international act was a run-out in the 2019 World Cup semi-final. He retired on August 15, 2020 — India's Independence Day.

players.name: Rohit Sharma
clues: Debuted in 2007 as a middle-order batter before becoming a prolific opener.
A right-hand batter who has scored three double centuries in ODI cricket.
Captained India in the T20 World Cup 2024.
Holds the record for the highest individual score in ODI cricket (264).
Captained a franchise in Mumbai to five IPL titles.
Known as 'Hitman' and wears jersey number 45.
players.funFact: He scored 264 against Sri Lanka in 2014 — the highest individual ODI score — hitting 33 fours and 9 sixes.

players.name: Jasprit Bumrah
clues: Debuted in international cricket in 2016 in a T20I.
A right-arm fast bowler with an unorthodox bowling action.
Became the fastest Indian pacer to reach 100 Test wickets.
Known for devastating yorkers at the death, especially in IPL.
Plays for a franchise in Mumbai in the IPL.
Wears jersey number 93 and has become India's premier fast bowler across formats.
players.funFact: His unique sling-arm bowling action was considered unusual but is now one of the most feared in world cricket. He's also taken a Test hat-trick.

players.name: Ravindra Jadeja
clues: Debuted in 2009 in an ODI and is known as one of the best fielders in world cricket.
A left-hand batting all-rounder who bowls slow left-arm orthodox spin.
From the Saurashtra cricket team in domestic cricket.
Known for sword celebrations after milestones on the field.
Played for Chennai Super Kings and is a key part of their squad.
Known as 'Sir Jadeja' and wears jersey number 8.
players.funFact: His sword celebration is inspired by Rajput warriors. He became one of only a few cricketers to score a century and take 5 wickets in the same Test.

players.name: Shane Warne
clues: Debuted in 1992 and is considered the greatest leg-spin bowler of all time.
An Australian leg-break bowler who took over 700 Test wickets.
Bowled the 'Ball of the Century' to dismiss Mike Gatting in the 1993 Ashes.
Captained a franchise to victory in the inaugural IPL season in 2008.
Played county cricket for Hampshire in England.
Known as the 'King of Spin' and wore jersey number 23.
players.funFact: His 'Ball of the Century' to Mike Gatting at Old Trafford in 1993 was his very first ball in Ashes cricket. It pitched outside leg stump and hit the top of off.

players.name: Ricky Ponting
clues: Debuted in 1995 and scored over 13,000 runs in both Tests and ODIs.
A right-hand batter from Tasmania who was one of the best pull-shot players ever.
Captained Australia to two consecutive World Cup wins (2003 and 2007).
Second highest run-scorer in Test cricket for Australia behind Allan Border.
Played for Mumbai Indians as a player and later became a coach in the IPL.
Known as 'Punter' and wore jersey number 14.
players.funFact: He won three World Cups as a player (1999, 2003, 2007) — more than any other cricketer in history.

players.name: Sir Donald Bradman
clues: Debuted in 1928 and retired in 1948, playing only Test cricket.
A right-hand batter with a Test batting average of 99.94.
An Australian who needed just 4 runs in his final Test innings to average 100.
Scored 29 Test centuries in just 52 matches.
Widely regarded as the greatest batsman in the history of cricket.
Known simply as 'The Don'.
players.funFact: In his final Test innings, he was bowled for a duck by Eric Hollies. Had he scored just 4 runs, his career average would have been exactly 100.

players.name: Glenn McGrath
clues: Debuted in 1993 and was renowned for metronomic line and length.
A right-arm fast-medium bowler who took over 560 Test wickets.
An Australian who was the key strike bowler in multiple Ashes series.
Took 71 wickets in World Cup matches — a record at the time of his retirement.
Played his entire domestic career for New South Wales.
Known as 'Pigeon' for his tall, thin build.
players.funFact: He was famous for predicting his match figures before a series. Before the 1997 Ashes, he predicted he would get 8 wickets in the first Test — and nearly did.

players.name: Adam Gilchrist
clues: Debuted in 1996 and redefined wicketkeeper-batting in Test cricket.
A left-hand batting wicketkeeper from Australia.
Scored a 149-ball 149 in the 2007 World Cup final with a squash ball inside his glove.
Known for explosive batting at number seven in the Test lineup.
Captained Deccan Chargers to IPL victory in 2009.
Known as 'Gilly' — one of the greatest wicketkeeper-batters ever.
players.funFact: He famously walked when he knew he was out, even if not given by the umpire, earning immense respect for sportsmanship.

players.name: Steve Smith
clues: Debuted in 2010 initially as a leg-spinning all-rounder before becoming a top-order batter.
A right-hand batter with an unorthodox technique and fidgety mannerisms at the crease.
An Australian who has one of the highest Test batting averages in the modern era.
Served a one-year ban from international cricket in 2018.
Scored 774 runs in the 2019 Ashes series in England.
Known as 'Smudge' and wears jersey number 49.
players.funFact: He started his international career as a leg-spinner batting at number 8 before transforming into one of the best Test batters of his generation.

players.name: Pat Cummins
clues: Debuted in 2011 as a teenager but injuries delayed his career for several years.
A right-arm fast bowler who became the number one Test bowler in the world.
An Australian who captained the team to World Cup victory in 2023.
Rose to become Australia's 47th Test captain.
Captained Kolkata Knight Riders in the IPL.
Wore jersey number 30 and became one of Australia's most successful captains.
players.funFact: After debuting as an 18-year-old with a match-winning performance, he missed nearly six years of Test cricket due to injuries before making a remarkable comeback.

players.name: Mitchell Starc
clues: Debuted in 2010 and is one of the fastest left-arm bowlers in cricket history.
A left-arm fast bowler known for swinging yorkers.
An Australian who holds the record for most wickets in a single World Cup (27 in 2015).
Has taken multiple five-wicket hauls in Ashes cricket.
Was bought for a record IPL auction price by Kolkata Knight Riders in 2024.
Wears jersey number 56 and is known for his devastating new-ball spells.
players.funFact: He was the Player of the Tournament in the 2015 World Cup, where Australia won on home soil, taking 22 wickets at an average of 10.18.

players.name: Brian Lara
clues: Debuted in 1990 and is the only batsman to score 400 not out in a Test innings.
A left-hand batter from the Caribbean with an elegant style.
Held the record for highest Test score twice (375 and then 400*).
Also held the record for highest first-class score: 501 not out for Warwickshire.
Represented Trinidad and Tobago in domestic cricket.
Known as 'The Prince' of Trinidad.
players.funFact: He scored 400 not out against England in Antigua in 2004, breaking Matthew Hayden's record of 380, and reclaiming the record he had first set with 375.

players.name: Sir Viv Richards
clues: Debuted in 1974 and was part of the dominant West Indies team of the 1970s-80s.
A right-hand batter from Antigua known for destructive, fearless batting.
Captained the West Indies and never lost a Test series as captain.
Scored the fastest Test century at the time — off 56 balls against England in 1986.
Played county cricket for Somerset and Glamorgan.
Known as 'King Viv' — widely regarded as one of the most intimidating batsmen ever.
players.funFact: He famously never wore a helmet throughout his career, even against the fastest bowlers in the world, as a statement of dominance.

players.name: Curtly Ambrose
clues: Debuted in 1988 and took 405 Test wickets at an average of 20.99.
A tall right-arm fast bowler from the Caribbean who generated steep bounce.
Took 6 wickets for 24 runs against England at Port of Spain in 1994.
Formed a devastating bowling partnership with Courtney Walsh.
Played county cricket for Northamptonshire in England.
Known as 'Big Bird' due to his 6'7" frame.
players.funFact: He was a basketball player before turning to cricket and originally wanted to be a musician. He now plays bass guitar in a band.

players.name: Chris Gayle
clues: Debuted in 1999 and became one of the most destructive T20 batters in history.
A left-hand batter from Jamaica who played franchise cricket worldwide.
Scored the first ever triple century in Test cricket for the West Indies (317 vs SA).
Holds the record for the highest individual score in T20 cricket: 175* off 66 balls.
Played for multiple IPL franchises including one based in Bangalore.
Known as the 'Universe Boss' and wore jersey number 333.
players.funFact: He scored 175* off just 66 balls for RCB against Pune Warriors in 2013 — the highest individual score in IPL history, hitting 17 sixes.

players.name: James Anderson
clues: Debuted in 2003 and bowled well into his 40s at the highest level.
A right-arm fast-medium swing bowler from England.
The highest wicket-taker among fast bowlers in Test cricket history.
Took over 700 Test wickets, all while playing in pace-unfriendly English conditions.
Played his entire domestic career for Lancashire.
Known as 'Jimmy' and wore jersey number 9.
players.funFact: He retired in 2024 at age 41, having become the most prolific fast bowler in Test history with 704 wickets — and he never played a single IPL match.

players.name: Ben Stokes
clues: Debuted in 2011 and became one of cricket's greatest match-winners.
A left-hand batting all-rounder who bowls right-arm fast-medium.
Played one of the greatest Ashes innings ever: 135* at Headingley in 2019.
Was Player of the Match in the 2019 World Cup final at Lord's.
Born in New Zealand but played for England, representing Durham domestically.
Known as 'Stokesy' and wears jersey number 55.
players.funFact: In the 2019 World Cup final, he accidentally deflected a throw to the boundary for 6 overthrows, helping England tie the match before winning in the Super Over.

players.name: Joe Root
clues: Debuted in 2012 and quickly became one of the 'Fab Four' batters of his generation.
A right-hand batter from Yorkshire known for elegant strokeplay.
England's highest run-scorer in Test cricket history.
Captained England in Test cricket from 2017 to 2022.
One of the 'Fab Four' alongside Kohli, Smith, and Williamson.
Known as 'Rooty' and wears jersey number 66.
players.funFact: He overtook Sir Alastair Cook's record to become England's all-time leading Test run-scorer, doing so with a characteristic sweep shot.

players.name: Kevin Pietersen
clues: Debuted in 2005 and made an immediate impact in the famous Ashes series win.
A right-hand batter born in South Africa who played for England.
Famous for his audacious switch-hit shot against spin bowlers.
Scored a century on Ashes debut and was Player of the Series in 2005.
Played for Delhi and Bangalore franchises in the IPL.
Known as 'KP' and was one of the most flamboyant batters of his era.
players.funFact: He invented the 'switch hit' — changing from a right-hander to a left-hander mid-delivery — and played it against world-class spin bowlers with remarkable success.

players.name: Wasim Akram
clues: Debuted in 1985 and is regarded as the greatest left-arm fast bowler in cricket history.
A left-arm fast bowler from Pakistan who mastered reverse swing.
Took over 900 international wickets across Tests and ODIs.
Was instrumental in Pakistan's 1992 World Cup victory.
Played county cricket for Lancashire and Hampshire in England.
Known as the 'Sultan of Swing'.
players.funFact: He could swing the ball both ways at high pace, and his two wickets in the 1992 World Cup final destroyed England's top order, securing Pakistan's only World Cup win.

players.name: Shahid Afridi
clues: Debuted in 1996 and once held the record for the fastest ODI century (37 balls).
A right-hand batting all-rounder who bowled leg-breaks for Pakistan.
Known for explosive, high-risk batting and six-hitting ability.
Hit 351 sixes in ODI cricket — a record at the time of his retirement.
Led Pakistan as captain in the 2011 World Cup semi-final.
Known as 'Boom Boom' and wore jersey number 10.
players.funFact: On his ODI debut in 1996, the 16-year-old smashed the fastest ODI century off just 37 balls against Sri Lanka. The record stood for 18 years.

players.name: Babar Azam
clues: Debuted in 2015 and quickly rose to become one of the 'Fab Five' batters in world cricket.
A right-hand batter known for classical, elegant cover drives.
The only batter to be ranked number one across all three formats simultaneously.
Captained Pakistan in the 2022 T20 World Cup final.
Represented Karachi Kings in the Pakistan Super League.
Wears jersey number 56 and is Pakistan's premier batter of this generation.
players.funFact: In 2021, he became the only male cricketer to simultaneously top the ICC rankings in all three formats — Tests, ODIs, and T20Is.

players.name: Imran Khan
clues: Debuted in 1971 and captained his team for over a decade.
A right-arm fast bowling all-rounder from Pakistan.
Led his country to their first and only World Cup victory in 1992.
Took 362 Test wickets and scored over 3800 Test runs.
Played county cricket for Worcestershire and Sussex in England.
Captained the 1992 World Cup winning side and later entered politics.
players.funFact: His famous speech after winning the 1992 World Cup — 'Cornered tigers are the most dangerous' — became one of cricket's most iconic moments.

players.name: AB de Villiers
clues: Debuted in 2004 and could play 360-degree shots all around the ground.
A right-hand batter from South Africa who also kept wicket occasionally.
Scored the fastest ODI century of all time — off just 31 balls.
One of the greatest IPL players, forming a legendary partnership with Virat Kohli at RCB.
Played for Bangalore in the IPL and was their most impactful overseas batter.
Known as 'Mr. 360' and wore jersey number 17.
players.funFact: His 31-ball century against the West Indies in 2015 included 16 sixes and remains the fastest ODI hundred in history.

players.name: Dale Steyn
clues: Debuted in 2004 and spent the most weeks ranked as ICC's No. 1 Test bowler.
A right-arm fast bowler from South Africa known for searing pace and swing.
South Africa's highest wicket-taker in Test cricket.
Took 439 Test wickets at an average under 23.
Played for multiple IPL teams including franchises in Bangalore and Hyderabad.
Known as 'Steyn Gun' and wore jersey number 8.
players.funFact: He held the number one ranking in ICC Test bowling rankings for a record 263 weeks. His pace and swing combination was considered unplayable on helpful pitches.

players.name: Jacques Kallis
clues: Debuted in 1995 and is statistically the greatest all-rounder in cricket history.
A right-hand batter who also bowled right-arm fast-medium for South Africa.
Scored over 13,000 Test runs AND took over 290 Test wickets.
One of only a few players to score 10,000+ runs and take 250+ wickets in Tests.
Played for Kolkata Knight Riders in the IPL.
Often called the most complete cricketer of his generation.
players.funFact: He holds the unique distinction of scoring over 25,000 international runs and taking over 570 international wickets — a double no other cricketer has achieved.

players.name: Hashim Amla
clues: Debuted in 2004 and became the fastest to 2000, 3000, 4000, 5000, 6000, and 7000 ODI runs.
A right-hand batter from South Africa with a distinctive long beard.
The first South African to score a triple century in Test cricket (311* vs England).
Scored 28 ODI centuries with a remarkable strike rate for his era.
Played for KwaZulu-Natal and the Dolphins in South African domestic cricket.
Known for graceful timing and was the fastest to many ODI run milestones.
players.funFact: He scored 311 not out against England at The Oval in 2012, becoming the first South African to score a Test triple century, batting for over 13 hours.

players.name: Kumar Sangakkara
clues: Debuted in 2000 and scored over 28,000 international runs across formats.
A left-hand batting wicketkeeper from Sri Lanka.
Scored four consecutive ODI centuries in the 2015 World Cup.
Holds the record for most Test dismissals by a wicketkeeper from the subcontinent.
Played for multiple IPL franchises and in county cricket for Surrey and Durham.
Known as 'Sanga' and wore jersey number 11.
players.funFact: He delivered a powerful MCC Spirit of Cricket Lecture in 2011 at Lord's, widely regarded as one of the finest speeches ever given by a cricketer.

players.name: Muttiah Muralitharan
clues: Debuted in 1992 and holds the record for most wickets in both Test and ODI cricket.
A right-arm off-break bowler from Sri Lanka with a unique action.
Took 800 Test wickets — more than any other bowler in history.
Inventor of the 'doosra' delivery that turns the opposite way.
Played for Chennai Super Kings in the IPL.
Known simply as 'Murali' and holds virtually every bowling record.
players.funFact: He took his 800th and final Test wicket with the last ball of his Test career against India in 2010, finishing with the greatest wicket tally in cricket history.

players.name: Lasith Malinga
clues: Debuted in 2004 and is known for his unorthodox sling-arm bowling action.
A right-arm fast bowler from Sri Lanka with distinctive curly hair.
The only bowler to take four wickets in four consecutive balls in international cricket — twice.
The highest wicket-taker in the history of T20 internationals.
A key player for Mumbai Indians across multiple IPL seasons.
Known as 'Slinga Malinga' for his round-arm sling action.
players.funFact: He took four wickets in four consecutive balls against South Africa in the 2007 World Cup and repeated the feat in a T20I — the only bowler to do so twice in internationals.

players.name: Mahela Jayawardene
clues: Debuted in 1997 and scored over 25,000 international runs.
A right-hand batter from Sri Lanka known for wristy elegance.
Scored 374 in a Test against South Africa — the highest by a Sri Lankan.
Scored a century in the 2011 World Cup final in a losing cause.
Now coaches in the IPL, having previously played for Delhi and Punjab franchises.
Known for his graceful cover drive and tactical acumen, later becoming a top cricket coach.
players.funFact: His 374 against South Africa in 2006 came in a record Test partnership of 624 with Kumar Sangakkara — the highest partnership in Test history.

players.name: Kane Williamson
clues: Debuted in 2010 and is one of the 'Fab Four' batters of his generation.
A right-hand batter from New Zealand known for calm, composed batting.
Captained his country to the final of both the 2019 and 2021 World Cups.
New Zealand's highest run-scorer in Test cricket.
Captained Sunrisers Hyderabad in the IPL.
One of the 'Fab Four' alongside Kohli, Smith, and Root, wearing jersey number 22.
players.funFact: He was on the losing side of the 2019 World Cup final despite the match ending in a tie, as England won on boundary count — widely considered the greatest cricket match ever.

players.name: Sir Richard Hadlee
clues: Debuted in 1973 and was the first bowler to take 400 Test wickets.
A right-arm fast-medium bowler from New Zealand who could also bat.
Took 431 Test wickets — a record that stood for years.
Played county cricket for Nottinghamshire, helping them win championships.
His father Walter and brothers Dayle and Barry also played for New Zealand.
Known as 'Paddles' — New Zealand's greatest ever cricketer.
players.funFact: He was the first bowler to reach 400 Test wickets, and in 1985-86, he single-handedly won a series for New Zealand against Australia with 33 wickets.

players.name: Trent Boult
clues: Debuted in 2011 and is one of New Zealand's finest left-arm fast bowlers.
A left-arm fast bowler known for swinging the new ball both ways.
Took a hat-trick in the 2019 World Cup semi-final against India.
Played key roles in New Zealand reaching two consecutive World Cup finals.
Played for Mumbai Indians, Rajasthan Royals, and Delhi Capitals in the IPL.
Wears jersey number 18 for New Zealand.
players.funFact: His hat-trick in the 2019 World Cup semi-final against India at Old Trafford dismantled the Indian top order and set up one of cricket's biggest upsets.

players.name: Rashid Khan
clues: Debuted in 2015 as a teenager and became the youngest Test captain in history.
A right-arm leg-break bowler from Afghanistan.
The youngest player to be ranked No. 1 in the ICC T20I bowling rankings.
Plays T20 franchise cricket worldwide and is a top pick in every league auction.
Captained Gujarat Titans in the IPL.
Wears jersey number 19 and is Afghanistan's most famous cricketer.
players.funFact: He became captain of Afghanistan at age 20, making him the youngest Test captain in cricket history. He's played in over 10 different T20 leagues worldwide.

players.name: Shakib Al Hasan
clues: Debuted in 2006 and has been ranked the No. 1 all-rounder by the ICC.
A left-hand batting all-rounder who bowls slow left-arm orthodox spin.
Bangladesh's greatest ever cricketer by most measures.
Has been the No. 1 ranked Test all-rounder on multiple occasions.
Played for Kolkata Knight Riders and Sunrisers Hyderabad in the IPL.
Wears jersey number 75 and is Bangladesh's all-time leading wicket-taker in Tests.
players.funFact: He has scored over 4000 Test runs and taken over 200 Test wickets — a truly rare double for a Bangladeshi cricketer in a team that often struggles in Tests.

players.name: Sunil Gavaskar
clues: Debuted in 1971 and was the first batter to score 10,000 Test runs.
A right-hand opening batter from India known for compact technique.
Scored 774 runs in his debut Test series against the West Indies.
Held the record for most Test centuries (34) before Sachin Tendulkar broke it.
Represented Mumbai (then Bombay) in domestic cricket.
Known as 'Sunny' or 'Little Master' — India's original batting great.
players.funFact: On his debut series in the West Indies in 1971, he scored 774 runs including four centuries and a double century — one of the greatest debut performances ever.

players.name: Kapil Dev
clues: Debuted in 1978 and was India's greatest fast-bowling all-rounder.
A right-arm fast-medium bowler who could also bat aggressively.
Captained India to their first World Cup victory in 1983.
Played a famous innings of 175* against Zimbabwe in the 1983 World Cup.
Represented Haryana in domestic cricket.
Known as the 'Haryana Hurricane' — India's first great pace-bowling captain.
players.funFact: His 175 not out against Zimbabwe in the 1983 World Cup was not televised, yet it's considered one of the most important innings in Indian cricket history. It saved India from elimination.

players.name: Rahul Dravid
clues: Debuted in 1996 and faced over 31,000 balls in Test cricket — more than any other batter.
A right-hand batter from India known for incredible patience and technique.
Scored over 13,000 Test runs with an average above 52.
Captained Rajasthan Royals in the IPL before becoming India's head coach.
Represented Karnataka in domestic cricket.
Known as 'The Wall' for his impenetrable defense.
players.funFact: He spent 44,152 minutes batting in Test cricket — the equivalent of over 30 full days. His ability to bat time earned him the nickname 'The Wall'.

players.name: Anil Kumble
clues: Debuted in 1990 and took over 600 Test wickets.
A right-arm leg-break bowler from India who relied on accuracy over spin.
One of only two bowlers to take all 10 wickets in a Test innings (10/74 vs Pakistan).
India's highest wicket-taker in Test cricket with 619 wickets.
Played for Royal Challengers Bangalore and later coached the Indian team.
Known as 'Jumbo' — only the second bowler to take 10 wickets in a Test innings.
players.funFact: He bowled with a broken jaw and a bandaged face against the West Indies in 2002, refusing to leave the field — epitomizing his fighting spirit.

players.name: Yuvraj Singh
clues: Debuted in 2000 and hit six sixes in an over in the inaugural T20 World Cup.
A left-hand batting all-rounder from India.
Player of the Tournament in the 2011 Cricket World Cup.
Hit Stuart Broad for six sixes in one over at the 2007 T20 World Cup.
Overcame cancer to return to international cricket.
Known as 'Yuvi' and wore jersey number 12.
players.funFact: He hit six consecutive sixes off Stuart Broad in the 2007 T20 World Cup, scoring the fastest T20I fifty (12 balls). He was later diagnosed with cancer but made a heroic comeback.

players.name: Harbhajan Singh
clues: Debuted in 1998 and was the first Indian to take a hat-trick in Test cricket.
A right-arm off-break bowler from Punjab.
Took 32 wickets in India's famous home series win against Australia in 2001.
Took a hat-trick against Australia at Kolkata in 2001 during an iconic Test match.
Played for Mumbai Indians across multiple IPL seasons.
Known as 'The Turbanator' and wore jersey number 3.
players.funFact: His hat-trick against Australia in the historic 2001 Kolkata Test — where India won after following on — is considered one of the greatest moments in cricket history.

players.name: Virender Sehwag
clues: Debuted in 1999 and is the only Indian to score a triple century in Test cricket — twice.
A right-hand opening batter known for fearless, aggressive batting.
Scored 309 against Pakistan and 319 against South Africa in Tests.
Transformed Test cricket opening by attacking from ball one.
Captained Delhi Daredevils in the IPL.
Known as 'Nawab of Najafgarh' — the most destructive Test opener of his era.
players.funFact: He scored 293 against Sri Lanka and was disappointed because he thought he would get another triple century. He's the only Indian with two Test triple hundreds (309 and 319).

players.name: Suresh Raina
clues: Debuted in 2005 and was one of the most consistent performers in IPL history.
A left-hand batter from Uttar Pradesh.
The first Indian to score a century in all three formats of international cricket.
Was the leading run-scorer in IPL history for a long period.
Spent most of his IPL career with Chennai Super Kings.
Known as 'Mr. IPL' or 'Chinna Thala' (Little Leader) and wore jersey number 3.
players.funFact: He retired from international cricket on the same day as MS Dhoni (August 15, 2020), showing their deep bond as CSK teammates and friends.

players.name: David Warner
clues: Debuted in 2009 as the first Australian to play international cricket without a first-class match.
A left-hand opening batter known for explosive batting.
An Australian who served a one-year ban in 2018 alongside Steve Smith.
Won the Orange Cap (most IPL runs) three times with Sunrisers Hyderabad.
Captained Sunrisers Hyderabad to their only IPL title in 2016.
Wears jersey number 31 and was one of the most prolific IPL overseas batters.
players.funFact: He was selected for Australia's T20I team directly from club cricket without having played a single first-class match — the first Australian to do so in over 130 years.

players.name: Sir Ian Botham
clues: Debuted in 1977 and is considered England's greatest all-rounder.
A right-arm fast-medium bowling all-rounder who could change matches single-handedly.
Scored 149 not out at Headingley in the 1981 Ashes — one of cricket's greatest innings.
The 1981 Ashes series was nicknamed after him.
Played county cricket for Somerset, Worcestershire, and Durham.
Known as 'Beefy' — the 1981 Ashes are often called 'Botham's Ashes'.
players.funFact: The 1981 Ashes Test at Headingley is considered the greatest Test match ever. England were following on and bookmakers offered 500/1 against England winning — then Botham scored 149*.

players.name: Andrew Flintoff
clues: Debuted in 1998 and was the hero of England's 2005 Ashes victory.
A right-arm fast bowling all-rounder from Lancashire.
Named Player of the Series in the 2005 Ashes — widely regarded as the best Ashes ever.
Famous for consoling a devastated Brett Lee after the Edgbaston Test in 2005.
Played a season for Chennai Super Kings in the IPL.
Known as 'Freddie' — the face of England cricket in the mid-2000s.
players.funFact: The iconic photograph of him consoling Brett Lee at the end of the 2005 Edgbaston Test (which England won by 2 runs) is considered one of cricket's greatest sporting gestures.

players.name: Mitchell Johnson
clues: Debuted in 2005 and terrorized England in the 2013-14 Ashes with 37 wickets.
A left-arm fast bowler from Australia known for extreme pace and a handlebar moustache.

players.name: Shoaib Akhtar
clues: Debuted in 1997 and was the first bowler to break the 100 mph barrier in cricket.
A right-arm fast bowler from Pakistan who generated extreme pace.
Bowled at 161.3 km/h (100.2 mph) against England in the 2003 World Cup.
Known for a long, dramatic run-up and express pace.
Played for Kolkata Knight Riders in the IPL.
Known as the 'Rawalpindi Express' — the fastest bowler in cricket history.
players.funFact: He bowled the fastest delivery ever recorded in cricket — 161.3 km/h (100.2 mph) — during the 2003 World Cup against England in South Africa.

players.name: Misbah-ul-Haq
clues: Debuted in 2002 and captained Pakistan for a long period despite being a late bloomer.
A right-hand batter known for stabilizing innings and calm captaincy.

players.name: Shaheen Shah Afridi
clues: Debuted in 2018 as a teenager and quickly became Pakistan's pace spearhead.
A tall left-arm fast bowler known for devastating inswing to right-handers.

Captained Lahore Qalandars in the Pakistan Super League.
One of the tallest fast bowlers in current cricket, generating steep bounce.

players.name: Matthew Hayden
clues: Debuted in 1994 and was one of the most intimidating opening batters in cricket.
A left-hand batter from Queensland known for his imposing physique and front-foot play.
Held the record for the highest individual Test score (380 vs Zimbabwe) before Brian Lara.
Part of one of the greatest opening partnerships in Test history with Justin Langer.

Known as 'Haydos' — a dominant opener who loved to attack from ball one.

players.name: Marnus Labuschagne
clues: Debuted in 2018 and became the world's No. 1 Test batter with remarkable consistency.

Wears jersey number 71 and is known for his quirky personality and leave technique.

players.name: Sunil Narine
clues: Debuted in 2012 and became one of the most mysterious spin bowlers in T20 cricket.
A right-arm off-break bowler from the West Indies with a unique action.

Was Player of the Tournament when KKR won the IPL title.
Known for his mystery spin and transformation into a T20 batting powerhouse at KKR.

players.name: Andre Russell
clues: Debuted in 2011 and is one of the most destructive all-rounders in T20 cricket.
A right-hand batting all-rounder from Jamaica who bowls right-arm fast.

A key player for Kolkata Knight Riders across many IPL seasons.
Won the MVP award in the IPL multiple times.
Known as 'Muscle Russell' or 'Dre Russ' — a T20 franchise cricket superstar.
players.funFact: He has one of the highest strike rates in IPL history and has won matches for KKR from seemingly impossible situations with his raw hitting power.

players.name: Kieron Pollard
clues: Debuted in 2007 and is one of the most experienced T20 players in world cricket.
A right-hand batting all-rounder from Trinidad known for powerful hitting.
Hit 6 sixes in an over in a T20I against Sri Lanka's Akila Dananjaya.
Was a mainstay at Mumbai Indians for over a decade.
Captained the West Indies in limited-overs cricket.
Wore jersey number 55 for Mumbai Indians — one of their longest-serving overseas players.
players.funFact: He hit 6 sixes in one over off Akila Dananjaya in a T20I in 2021, joining an exclusive club of batters to achieve this feat in international cricket.

players.name: Shubman Gill
clues: Debuted in 2019 and quickly became India's future batting star.
A right-hand batter from Punjab with elegant strokeplay.
Captain of India's U-19 World Cup campaign before graduating to the senior team.
Has scored double centuries in ODIs at a young age.
Played for Gujarat Titans and Kolkata Knight Riders in the IPL.
Wears jersey number 77 and is seen as the next great Indian batter.
players.funFact: He scored a match-winning 91 in the fourth innings of the historic Gabba Test in 2021, helping India breach Australia's fortress.

players.name: Rishabh Pant
clues: Debuted in 2017 and is one of the most exciting wicketkeeper-batters in world cricket.
A left-hand batter from Delhi known for audacious shot-making.
Scored a century at the Gabba to help India win the 2021 Border-Gavaskar series.
The youngest Indian wicketkeeper to score a Test century.
Captained Delhi Capitals in the IPL.
Wears jersey number 17 and survived a serious car accident in 2022.
players.funFact: He survived a life-threatening car accident in December 2022, and his remarkable recovery and return to cricket inspired millions of fans.

players.name: Hardik Pandya
clues: Debuted in 2016 and became India's premier fast-bowling all-rounder.
A right-hand batting all-rounder who bowls right-arm fast-medium.
Captained Gujarat Titans to the IPL title in their debut season (2022).
Played a crucial role in India's 2024 T20 World Cup triumph.
From Baroda in domestic cricket, he and his brother Krunal both play cricket.
Wears jersey number 33 and led a new IPL franchise to the title in their first year.
players.funFact: He captained the Gujarat Titans to the IPL title in their very first season in 2022 — one of the most remarkable achievements in IPL history.

players.name: Ravichandran Ashwin
clues: Debuted in 2010 and is one of the quickest bowlers to reach 500 Test wickets.
A right-arm off-break bowler from Tamil Nadu who can also bat.
India's second-highest wicket-taker in Test cricket.
Known for innovating the 'carrom ball' delivery in international cricket.
Played for Chennai Super Kings, Delhi Capitals, and Rajasthan Royals in the IPL.
Wears jersey number 99 and is known for constant innovation in his bowling.
players.funFact: He invented and popularized the 'carrom ball' — flicked with the fingers like a carrom disc — adding a unique weapon to his already vast repertoire of spin deliveries.

players.name: KL Rahul
clues: Debuted in 2014 and is one of India's most versatile batters across formats.
A right-hand batter from Karnataka who also keeps wicket.
Scored the fastest IPL century (in 14 minutes, off 26 balls) in the 2020 season.
Won the Orange Cap in IPL 2020 while captaining Kings XI Punjab.
Captained Lucknow Super Giants in the IPL.
Wears jersey number 1 and has played for four different IPL franchises.
players.funFact: He hit the joint-fastest century in IPL history off just 26 balls for Kings XI Punjab against Royal Challengers Bangalore in 2020.

players.name: Glenn Maxwell
clues: Debuted in 2012 and is known as one of the most unorthodox batters in world cricket.
A right-hand batting all-rounder from Australia who bowls off-breaks.
Scored a double century (201*) in a World Cup match against Afghanistan in 2023.
Known for reverse sweeps, switch hits, and 360-degree shot-making.

Known as 'The Big Show' and wears jersey number 32.
players.funFact: His 201* against Afghanistan in the 2023 World Cup came after being injured and barely able to run. He hit his way to the highest World Cup score ever, largely in boundaries.

players.name: Nathan Lyon
clues: Debuted in 2011 and has taken over 500 Test wickets.
A right-arm off-break bowler from Australia.
Australia's most successful off-spinner in Test cricket history.

His teammates gave him the nickname 'GOAT' (Greatest of All Time).
Known as 'GOAT' or 'Garry' and wears jersey number 67.
players.funFact: Before becoming Australia's No. 1 spinner, he was working as a groundsman at the Adelaide Oval, mowing the same pitch he would later take hundreds of wickets on.

players.name: Dennis Lillee
clues: Debuted in 1971 and formed one of the most feared bowling partnerships in cricket history.
A right-arm fast bowler from Australia with a classic bowling action.

Overcame serious back injuries to return to fast bowling at the highest level.
Known for his fierce competitive spirit and iconic moustache.
players.funFact: He once tried to use an aluminium bat in a Test match against England, refusing to change it until his captain Greg Chappell convinced him, causing a famous delay.

players.name: Waqar Younis
clues: Debuted in 1989 and formed a legendary fast-bowling partnership with Wasim Akram.
A right-arm fast bowler from Pakistan known for reverse-swinging yorkers.

players.funFact: The Wasim-Waqar partnership is considered the greatest fast-bowling duo in cricket history. Together they took over 800 wickets in ODI cricket alone.

players.name: Inzamam-ul-Haq

Known as 'Inzi' — famous for his run-outs due to poor running between wickets.
players.funFact: He once chased a spectator into the stands with a bat after being heckled during a match in Canada in 1997, resulting in a suspension.

players.name: Graeme Smith
clues: Debuted in 2002 and became the youngest Test captain for South Africa at age 22.
A left-hand opening batter known for his strong will and determination.
South Africa's most successful Test captain, never losing a series at home.
Scored a double century (277) against England at Edgbaston in 2003.
Made South Africa the No. 1 Test team during his captaincy tenure.
The youngest ever South African Test captain, appointed at just 22 years old.
players.funFact: He famously batted with a broken hand against Australia in a 2009 Test, walking out to bat last to try to save the match — an incredible display of courage.

players.name: Kagiso Rabada
clues: Debuted in 2014 as a 19-year-old and quickly became one of the world's best fast bowlers.
A right-arm fast bowler from South Africa.
Won the Purple Cap (most wickets) in the IPL in 2020.
The youngest South African to take 200 Test wickets.
Played for Delhi Capitals and Punjab Kings in the IPL.
Wears jersey number 25 and is known as 'KG'.
players.funFact: He took 5 wickets on his ODI debut at the 2015 World Cup as a 19-year-old, including the wicket of the great Kumar Sangakkara.

players.name: Quinton de Kock
clues: Debuted in 2012 and is a destructive left-hand opening wicketkeeper-batter.
A South African who scored three consecutive ODI centuries against India on debut in India.

Was a key player for Mumbai Indians, helping them win the IPL title.
Played for Lucknow Super Giants in the IPL.
Wears jersey number 12 and scored three centuries in his first ODI series in India.
players.funFact: On his first ODI tour of India in 2013, he scored three consecutive centuries — becoming the youngest batter to achieve this feat in ODI history.

players.name: Allan Donald
clues: Debuted in 1992 (South Africa's return to international cricket) and was their first great fast bowler.
A right-arm fast bowler from South Africa.

Played county cricket for Warwickshire in England.
Known as 'White Lightning' for his express pace.
players.funFact: His 1998 Trent Bridge confrontation with Michael Atherton — where he repeatedly beat the bat without getting the wicket — is considered one of the greatest spells ever bowled.

players.name: Sanath Jayasuriya
clues: Debuted in 1989 and revolutionized ODI opening batting in the 1996 World Cup.
A left-hand batting all-rounder from Sri Lanka who bowled slow left-arm orthodox.

Player of the Tournament in the 1996 Cricket World Cup, which Sri Lanka won.
Sri Lanka's most capped ODI player with over 440 appearances.
Revolutionized the use of the first 15 overs in ODI cricket with his attacking approach.

players.name: Chaminda Vaas
clues: Debuted in 1994 and was Sri Lanka's most successful fast bowler.
A left-arm fast-medium bowler who could also bat usefully.

Sri Lanka's highest wicket-taker in ODI cricket.

players.funFact: He took a hat-trick with the very first three balls of a match against Bangladesh in the 2003 World Cup — the only time this has happened in World Cup history.

players.name: Daniel Vettori
clues: Debuted in 1997 at age 18 and became New Zealand's most capped Test player.
A slow left-arm orthodox bowler who was also a capable lower-order batter.

Captained New Zealand across all formats.

Known for his round glasses and intelligent bowling — NZ's greatest spin bowler.
players.funFact: He made his Test debut at 18 years old and went on to play 113 Tests for New Zealand — the most by any New Zealand cricketer.

players.name: Brendon McCullum
clues: Debuted in 2002 and was the first player to score a century in the first ever IPL match.
A wicketkeeper-batter from New Zealand known for explosive batting.

Captained New Zealand to the 2015 World Cup final.
Known as 'Baz' or 'BMac' — scored 158* in the very first IPL match ever played.
players.funFact: His 158* in the first ever IPL match (2008) set the tone for the entire tournament and remains one of the most iconic innings in IPL history.

players.name: Ross Taylor
clues: Debuted in 2006 and is New Zealand's highest run-scorer in international cricket.
A right-hand batter from New Zealand known for his pull shot.
Hit the winning runs in the 2021 World Test Championship final against India.
New Zealand's leading run-scorer in both Tests and ODIs at the time of his retirement.
Played for multiple IPL franchises across several seasons.
Known as 'Rosco' and wore jersey number 28.
players.funFact: He hit the winning runs to give New Zealand their first ICC trophy — the 2021 World Test Championship — against India at the Rose Bowl in Southampton.

players.name: Mushfiqur Rahim
clues: Debuted in 2005 at age 15 and became Bangladesh's most experienced cricketer.
A wicketkeeper-batter from Bangladesh.
The first Bangladeshi to score a double century in Test cricket.
Bangladesh's most prolific run-scorer in Test cricket.
Led Bangladesh's wicketkeeping duties for over 15 years.
Wears jersey number 15 and was Bangladesh's youngest ever Test cricketer.
players.funFact: He debuted at 15 years old and scored Bangladesh's first ever Test double century (200) against Sri Lanka, a landmark moment for Bangladesh cricket.

players.name: Tamim Iqbal
clues: Debuted in 2007 and is Bangladesh's most successful opening batter.
A left-hand batter from Bangladesh.
Bangladesh's highest run-scorer in ODI cricket.
Scored a century on his ODI debut against Zimbabwe.
Captained Bangladesh in ODI cricket.
Wears jersey number 28 and is the first Bangladeshi to score 5000 ODI runs.
players.funFact: He batted with a broken hand against India at the 2019 World Cup, refusing to retire hurt, showing remarkable courage for his country.

players.name: Mohammad Nabi
clues: Debuted in 2009 and is one of Afghanistan's most experienced cricketers.

One of the most sought-after T20 franchise cricketers from Afghanistan.

Known as the elder statesman of Afghan cricket alongside Rashid Khan.
players.funFact: He was part of the Afghanistan team that gained ODI and Test status, making him a pioneer of Afghan cricket on the world stage.

players.name: Marvan Atapattu
clues: Debuted in 1990 and scored six Test double centuries — the third most in history.

Despite his disastrous start, went on to average over 39 in Tests.

players.name: Andrew Symonds

Known for his exceptional fielding and athleticism.
Played for Deccan Chargers in the early IPL seasons.
Known as 'Roy' — famous for his dreadlocks, fishing, and all-round cricketing ability.

players.name: Zaheer Khan

Captained Kolkata Knight Riders in the IPL.
Known as 'Morgs' — born in Ireland but led England to World Cup glory.

players.name: Stuart Broad
clues: Debuted in 2006 and took over 600 Test wickets for England.

Took 8 wickets for 15 runs against Australia at Trent Bridge in 2015.

Wore jersey number 8 — took 8/15 in one of the most devastating Ashes spells ever.

players.name: Aravinda de Silva
clues: Debuted in 1984 and was the star of the 1996 World Cup final.
A right-hand batter from Sri Lanka known for dazzling strokeplay.
Scored an unbeaten century (107*) in the 1996 World Cup final against Australia.
Player of the Match in the 1996 World Cup final at Lahore.

Known as 'Mad Max' — scored one of the most famous World Cup final centuries.

players.name: Courtney Walsh

The first bowler to reach the milestone of 500 Test wickets.

players.name: Jason Holder
clues: Debuted in 2014 and became the youngest West Indian Test captain in the modern era.
A tall right-arm fast-medium bowling all-rounder from Barbados.

Played for Sunrisers Hyderabad and Rajasthan Royals in the IPL.
Wears jersey number 98 and was the ICC's No. 1 Test all-rounder.
players.funFact: At 6'7", he uses his height to generate steep bounce and has the rare ability to bat, bowl, and lead — making him West Indies' most dependable cricketer of his generation.

players.name: Malcolm Marshall

A right-arm fast bowler from Barbados who was relatively short for a fast bowler.

Part of the dominant West Indies pace quartet of the 1980s.

Known as 'Maco' — despite being 5'11", he was devastatingly quick.

players.name: Faf du Plessis
clues: Debuted in 2011 and was a match-winner for South Africa and in T20 leagues worldwide.
A right-hand batter from South Africa known for gutsy performances under pressure.

Captained South Africa in all three formats.

Known as 'Faf' and wears jersey number 18.
players.funFact: On his Test debut in 2012, he batted for over 6 hours, scoring 110* off 376 balls to save the match against Australia in Adelaide — one of the greatest debut innings.

players.name: Devon Conway

Moved from South Africa to New Zealand to pursue his cricket career.
Scored a double century at the 'Home of Cricket' in his very first Test match.
players.funFact: He scored 200 on his Test debut at Lord's in 2021 — only the seventh player in history to score a double century on Test debut, and the first at Lord's.

players.name: Mitchell Santner
clues: Debuted in 2015 and became an integral part of New Zealand's white-ball setup.
A left-hand batting all-rounder who bowls slow left-arm orthodox spin.

players.funFact: He went from being a relatively unknown New Zealand spinner to captaining one of the most storied IPL franchises in Chennai Super Kings.

players.name: Shai Hope
clues: Debuted in 2016 and is one of the West Indies' most consistent ODI batters.

players.name: Yashasvi Jaiswal

Scored a double century in only his third Test match.
Was the U-19 World Cup Player of the Tournament in 2020.

players.name: Jos Buttler

Wears jersey number 63 — scored the runs that won England their first World Cup.
players.funFact: He scored the winning runs in the Super Over of the 2019 World Cup final — the most dramatic finish in cricket history — diving to make his ground.

players.name: Jofra Archer

Known for his calm demeanor under extreme pressure.
Was bought by Mumbai Indians for a record sum at the IPL auction.

players.funFact: He bowled the Super Over in the 2019 World Cup final — in his debut international summer — with ice-cold composure, helping England win their first World Cup.

players.name: Rachin Ravindra

players.funFact: His name 'Rachin' is a combination of Rahul Dravid (Ra-) and Sachin Tendulkar (-chin), chosen by his Indian-origin father who admired both legends.

players.name: Travis Head
clues: Debuted in 2016 and became Australia's big-game performer in ICC events.

players.funFact: He scored match-winning centuries in the 2023 WTC final, 2023 Ashes, and 2023 World Cup final — earning a reputation as cricket's greatest big-game player.

players.name: Shahid Khan Afridi
clues: Debuted in 2012 and has been part of Afghanistan's rise in world cricket.
A left-arm fast bowler from Afghanistan — not to be confused with the Pakistani cricketer of similar name.
Has represented Afghanistan in both ODI and T20I cricket.
One of the earliest pace bowlers to represent Afghanistan at the international level.
Part of the Afghan bowling attack alongside Rashid Khan.
An Afghan left-arm pacer who shares his name with a famous Pakistani all-rounder.
players.funFact: Sharing a name with the iconic Pakistani all-rounder caused confusion in early scorecards, but he carved his own path as one of Afghanistan's pioneering pace bowlers.

players.name: Jonny Bairstow
clues: Debuted in 2011 and was at the center of one of cricket's biggest controversies at Lord's.
A right-hand batting wicketkeeper from Yorkshire.
Was controversially stumped by Alex Carey while wandering out of his crease in the 2023 Ashes.
Scored six Test centuries in a seven-match streak in 2022 under Bazball.
Played for Sunrisers Hyderabad and Punjab Kings in the IPL.
Known as 'YJB' — wears jersey number 51, son of former England keeper David Bairstow.
players.funFact: His father David Bairstow also played for Yorkshire and England. Jonny's controversial stumping at Lord's in the 2023 Ashes became one of the most debated incidents in cricket.

players.name: Rahul Tripathi
clues: Made his international debut in 2023 after years of stellar IPL performances.
A right-hand batter from Maharashtra known for clean hitting.
Was one of the most consistent Indian uncapped players in IPL history before getting called up.
Played for multiple IPL franchises including KKR and Sunrisers Hyderabad.
Known for his innovative shot-making in T20 cricket.
A late bloomer in international cricket — proved himself through consistent IPL performances.
players.funFact: He waited until he was 32 years old to make his India debut, proving that consistent IPL performances can eventually lead to international recognition.

players.name: Mohammed Shami
clues: Debuted in 2013 and became one of India's best seam bowlers across formats.
A right-arm fast-medium bowler from Bengal.
Took 7 wickets in the 2023 World Cup semi-final against New Zealand.
Known for his beautiful seam position and ability to swing the ball both ways.
Played for Gujarat Titans and Delhi Capitals in the IPL.
Wears jersey number 11 — took 24 wickets in the 2023 World Cup.
players.funFact: He took 24 wickets in the 2023 World Cup — the most by any bowler in that tournament — including a devastating 7-wicket haul in the semi-final against New Zealand.

players.name: David Gower
clues: Debuted in 1978 and was known for the most graceful batting in English cricket.
A left-hand batter who captained England and scored over 8,000 Test runs.
Led England to an Ashes victory in Australia in 1986-87.
England's leading Test run-scorer at the time of his retirement.
Played for Leicestershire and Hampshire in county cricket.
Known for supreme elegance — often described as the most stylish English batter of his era.
players.funFact: He once hired a Tiger Moth biplane to buzz over the ground during a match in Queensland, flying over his own teammates while they were fielding.

players.name: Michael Holding
clues: Debuted in 1975 and was one of the smoothest fast bowlers in cricket history.
A right-arm fast bowler from Jamaica with a silky, rhythmic run-up.
Took 14 wickets for 149 runs at The Oval in 1976 against England.
His bowling action was so smooth that the umpires couldn't hear his approach.
Part of the fearsome West Indian pace quartet of the late 1970s and 1980s.
Known as 'Whispering Death' because of his silent, graceful run-up.
players.funFact: His 14/149 at The Oval in 1976 is considered one of the greatest fast bowling displays ever. The umpire couldn't hear him approaching, hence the nickname 'Whispering Death'.

players.name: Mark Waugh
clues: Debuted in 1991 and was one of the most elegant batters in Australian cricket.
A right-hand batter from New South Wales — twin brother of a famous Australian captain.
Scored a century on his Test debut, replacing his twin brother in the team.
Known for exquisite slip catching and silky stroke play.
Played county cricket for Essex in England.
Known as 'Junior' — the twin brother of Australia's Test captain Steve Waugh.
players.funFact: He replaced his twin brother Steve in the Australian Test team for his debut and promptly scored a century against England. The twins played 108 Tests together.

players.name: Steve Waugh
clues: Debuted in 1985 and captained one of the most dominant teams in cricket history.
A right-hand batter from New South Wales known for mental toughness.
Captained Australia to a record 16 consecutive Test victories.
Twin brother of another Australian international cricketer.
Scored a famous last-ball century against England at the SCG in 2003.
Known as 'Tugga' or 'Ice Man' — one of Australia's greatest captains.
players.funFact: His century on the last ball of Day 2 at the SCG in 2003 — his last Ashes Test — is considered one of the most dramatic centuries in cricket history.

players.name: Shivnarine Chanderpaul
clues: Debuted in 1994 and played Test cricket for over 20 years.
A left-hand batter from Guyana with a unique crab-like stance.
Scored over 11,000 Test runs with an average above 51.
Known for his unorthodox stance where he faced the bowler almost chest-on.
Was the ICC Test Player of the Year in 2008.
Known as 'Tiger' — famous for his crab-like batting stance.
players.funFact: His crab-like stance — almost facing chest-on to the bowler — was one of the most unorthodox in cricket, yet he averaged over 51 in Tests across 164 matches.

players.name: Morne Morkel
clues: Debuted in 2006 and formed a potent pace trio with Steyn and Philander.
A tall right-arm fast bowler from South Africa at 6'5".
Took over 300 wickets in international cricket across formats.
Brother of another South African international cricketer (Albie Morkel).
Played for Kolkata Knight Riders and Delhi Daredevils in the IPL.
At 6'5", he used his height to generate extreme bounce.
players.funFact: He and his brother Albie both played international cricket for South Africa, with Morne being the tall fast bowler and Albie the hard-hitting all-rounder.

players.name: Mitchell Marsh
clues: Debuted in 2011 and became Australia's T20I captain.
A right-hand batting all-rounder who bowls right-arm fast-medium.
Son of former Australian cricketer Geoff Marsh and brother of Shaun Marsh.
Player of the Match in the 2021 T20 World Cup final.
Played for Delhi Capitals and Sunrisers Hyderabad in the IPL.
Known as 'Bison' — scored a match-winning 77* in the 2021 T20 World Cup final.
players.funFact: His father Geoff played 50 Tests for Australia and his brother Shaun also played international cricket, making the Marshes one of cricket's great family dynasties.

players.name: Alastair Cook
clues: Debuted in 2006 and is England's most capped Test player.
A left-hand opening batter who played 161 Tests for England.
Scored over 12,000 Test runs — England's record at the time.
Captained England to an Ashes victory in Australia in 2010-11.
Played his entire county career for Essex.
Known as 'Chef' — England's highest-ever Test run scorer and most capped player.
players.funFact: He scored a century in his final Test innings at The Oval in 2018, walking off to a standing ovation in one of cricket's most emotional farewells.

players.name: VVS Laxman
clues: Debuted in 1996 and played one of the greatest Test innings in cricket history.
A right-hand batter from Hyderabad known for wristy, elegant batting.
Scored 281 against Australia in the famous Kolkata Test of 2001.
His 281 at Eden Gardens helped India win after following on — only the third time in Test history.
Named after the Tirumala Venkateswara temple (VVS stands for Vangipurappu Venkata Sai).
Known as 'Very Very Special' — his 281 at Kolkata is considered one of the greatest Test innings ever.
players.funFact: His 281 at Eden Gardens in 2001 is ranked as one of the greatest innings in cricket history. India were following on and VVS batted for almost 10 hours to help India win by 171 runs.

players.name: Sourav Ganguly
clues: Debuted in 1996 with a century at Lord's on his Test debut.
A left-hand batter from Bengal who was one of India's most aggressive captains.
Famously waved his shirt on the Lord's balcony after India's NatWest Trophy win in 2002.
Transformed Indian cricket's attitude from passive to aggressive as captain.
Later became the President of the BCCI (Board of Control for Cricket in India).
Known as 'Dada' (elder brother) and 'Prince of Kolkata'.
players.funFact: His shirtless celebration on the Lord's balcony after the 2002 NatWest final is one of cricket's most iconic moments — a response to Andrew Flintoff doing the same in India.

players.name: Irfan Pathan
clues: Debuted in 2003 at age 19 and took a hat-trick in the first over of a Test against Pakistan.
A left-arm fast-medium bowling all-rounder from India.
The youngest Indian to take a Test hat-trick (at age 21).
His hat-trick came in the very first over of a Test match at Karachi in 2006.
Brother of another Indian cricketer, Yusuf Pathan.
Known for his Test hat-trick in the first over — the first ever in the opening over of a Test.
players.funFact: He took a hat-trick in the first over of a Test match against Pakistan in 2006 — the only hat-trick ever taken in the first over of a Test match in cricket history.

players.name: Suryakumar Yadav
clues: Debuted in 2021 and quickly became the world's No. 1 T20I batter.
A right-hand batter from Mumbai known for 360-degree shot-making.
Named ICC T20I Cricketer of the Year in 2022 and 2023.
His unorthodox shots include ramp shots over the keeper and flicks over mid-wicket.
Plays for Mumbai Indians in the IPL and is from Mumbai domestically.
Known as 'SKY' — the world's No. 1 T20I batter, wearing jersey number 63.
players.funFact: He waited until age 30 for his international debut, but once selected, he broke virtually every T20I batting record and was named the world's best T20I batter.

players.name: Younis Khan
clues: Debuted in 2000 and is Pakistan's highest run-scorer in Test cricket.
A right-hand batter known for playing long innings and converting fifties to centuries.
Scored over 10,000 Test runs — the only Pakistani to reach this milestone.
Captained Pakistan to the 2009 T20 World Cup victory.
Scored centuries in every Test-playing nation.
The only Pakistani cricketer to score 10,000 Test runs.
players.funFact: He scored Test centuries in every Test-playing nation — a remarkable achievement that showcased his adaptability to all conditions around the world.

players.name: Saeed Anwar
clues: Debuted in 1989 and held the record for the highest individual ODI score for 13 years.
A left-hand opening batter from Pakistan known for sublime elegance.
Scored 194 against India in Chennai in 1997 — then the highest individual ODI score.
His 194 was the ODI record before Sachin Tendulkar's 200* broke it in 2010.
Known for graceful drives and delicate touch.
His 194 against India in 1997 stood as the ODI record for 13 years.
players.funFact: His 194 against India in 1997 was so dominant that even Indian fans gave him a standing ovation. The record stood for 13 years until Tendulkar scored 200*.

players.name: Tim Southee
clues: Debuted in 2008 and became New Zealand's second-highest wicket-taker in Tests.
A right-arm fast-medium bowler from Northern Districts.
Took 7-64 on his Test debut against England at Napier as a 19-year-old.
New Zealand's all-time leading wicket-taker in T20I cricket.
Played for multiple IPL teams including Kolkata Knight Riders and CSK.
Wears jersey number 38 — took 7 wickets on debut and became NZ's T20I wicket king.
players.funFact: On his Test debut at 19, he took 7 wickets and scored 77 not out against England — one of the most impressive all-round Test debuts ever.

players.name: Dinesh Karthik
clues: Debuted in 2004 and had one of the longest international careers for an Indian wicketkeeper.
A right-hand batting wicketkeeper from Tamil Nadu.
Hit the last ball for six against Bangladesh to win the 2018 Nidahas Trophy final.
His last-ball six in the 2018 Nidahas Trophy is one of India's most celebrated T20 moments.
Captained Kolkata Knight Riders and played for Royal Challengers Bangalore.
Known as 'DK' — his Nidahas Trophy final six is one of Indian cricket's iconic moments.
players.funFact: His last-ball six against Bangladesh in the 2018 Nidahas Trophy final — after India was 34/3 chasing 167 — is considered one of the greatest finishes in T20I cricket.

players.name: Kuldeep Yadav
clues: Debuted in 2017 and is India's only regular left-arm wrist spinner.
A left-arm wrist spin bowler (chinaman) — a rare bowling type in cricket.
Took a hat-trick against Australia in an ODI in Kolkata in 2017.
One of the few left-arm wrist spinners in international cricket history.
Played for Kolkata Knight Riders and Delhi Capitals in the IPL.
Wears jersey number 23 — took a hat-trick against Australia as India's chinaman bowler.
players.funFact: Left-arm wrist spin (chinaman bowling) is one of cricket's rarest bowling types. He is India's first-choice exponent of this art, making him genuinely unique.

players.name: Ajinkya Rahane
clues: Debuted in 2011 and captained India to a historic series win in Australia.
A right-hand batter from Mumbai known for elegance and calmness under pressure.
Led India to a 2-1 series win in Australia in 2020-21 after Virat Kohli left the tour.
Known for performing better in overseas Tests than at home.
Captained Rajasthan Royals in the IPL.
Known as 'Jinx' — captained India to their most famous overseas Test series win.
players.funFact: He captained India to a 2-1 series win in Australia in 2020-21, rallying a depleted team after Kohli left for paternity leave and multiple players were injured.

players.name: Bhuvneshwar Kumar
clues: Debuted in 2012 and was India's premier swing bowler in white-ball cricket.
A right-arm medium-fast bowler from Uttar Pradesh.
Won the Purple Cap (most wickets) in the IPL in 2016 and 2017.
Known for prodigious swing with the new ball, especially in helpful conditions.
Spent his entire IPL career with Sunrisers Hyderabad.
Wears jersey number 15 — won back-to-back Purple Caps for Sunrisers Hyderabad.
players.funFact: He won the IPL Purple Cap in consecutive seasons (2016 and 2017) with Sunrisers Hyderabad, cementing his reputation as one of the best swing bowlers in Indian cricket.
